summary: There is no universal SAP Ariba keyboard shortcut for registering a buyer. Buyer setup is normally handled through tenant administration, role provisioning, or user management workflows.
key_risks: Keyboard shortcuts can differ by Ariba tenant and UI version
Buyer creation may require admin permissions
recommended_next_step: Use your Ariba admin or user-provisioning workflow to assign the buyer role, and check your tenant guide for the exact menu path.

summary: When a requisition number is generated, it can be used as the trigger for downstream procurement automation, tracking, and approval follow-up.
key_risks: The exact event name differs by tenant integration
Automation should respect approval and compliance rules
recommended_next_step: Send the requisition number to the local webhook endpoint so the system can record the event and run the configured automation action.

summary: Supplier onboarding usually needs validation, approval, and compliance review before the supplier becomes usable in procurement workflows.
key_risks: Using an unapproved supplier can violate procurement policy
Different regions may require tax, legal, or security checks
recommended_next_step: Verify the supplier master record and approval status before allowing it into the sourcing or buying flow.

summary: Requisition approval should follow the organization's policy thresholds, budget checks, and role-based approval chain.
key_risks: Skipping approval can create audit and compliance exposure
Threshold rules can differ across business units
recommended_next_step: Confirm the budget owner, threshold, and approval chain before releasing the requisition.

summary: Catalog and purchase order actions should follow approved supplier, contract, and policy controls before submission.
key_risks: Contract terms may require legal review
Using non-catalog items can require extra approvals
recommended_next_step: Check whether the item is catalog-enabled and whether the request maps to an existing approved contract.
